reason: Test-only; no production code touched. Adds tests/architecture/test_store_methods_have_production_callers.py, which pins every public SQL-store method that nothing under nora/ calls, with a reason and one of three shapes (read_back_affordance / deferred_consumer / defect). A full audit of the standing, knowledge, language and note tiers found 13 such methods plus 12 reverse-direction gaps (columns with no writer, tables with no store, a config key read nowhere), and the reading that survives all of them is that the CONTRACT SUITE was accepted as the completion gate: SqlNoteStore.record_wake has ~15 contract-test call sites and zero production ones, SqlTurnVerdictStore.read says outright it is 'present for the contract suite', and tag_trace_rederive.rebuild_state has a named test asserting that it raises. A green test measured that the verb WORKS; nothing measured that it is USED. This is NOT a to-do list and explicitly not an instruction to wire them up - most are deliberate read-back affordances with nothing to wire them to. It makes the inventory a checked artifact rather than one rediscovered every few weeks, and forces the next unwired method to be classified deliberately. Callers resolve by method name, which is only sound for the 99 of 120 names that are unique across store classes; the 21 shared names (read, recent, save, resolve, supersede, ...) are pinned as unchecked rather than assumed clean, and that list is asserted to equal the set the code actually shares. Both pins are checked in both directions, so wiring a method up or renaming one fails the gate instead of leaving a stale row.
